 Wisconsin DMV reminds voters to bring proper ID to polls
 October 19, 2026 by Daily Dodge 
 MADISON — The Wisconsin Department of Transportation Division of Motor Vehicles is reminding voters to make sure they have an acceptable form of identification before the Nov. 3 election.
 A Wisconsin driver’s license or identification card is among the most common forms of ID accepted at polling places. A federally compliant REAL ID is not required.
 Other acceptable forms of identification may include military and student ID cards. Voters can check whether their identification meets state requirements at bringit.wi.gov .
 Wisconsin residents who need an ID for voting can apply for one free of charge at a DMV Customer Service Center. U.S. citizens also may receive a free receipt valid for voting if their identification card is not ready in time for the election.
 For information about required documents or to find a DMV location, visit wisconsindmv.gov/idcards . Questions about obtaining an ID for voting can be directed to the DMV hotline at 844-588-1069.
